concepts.title: Monomials, Binomials, Trinomials and Polynomials
concepts.definition: Algebraic expressions are built from terms: one term is a monomial, two unlike terms make a binomial, three a trinomial, and many terms a polynomial; like terms - same variable parts - can be added or subtracted by combining coefficients.
concepts.formula: sum = coef_a + coef_b for like terms
concepts.key_idea: Name expressions by their term count; only like terms merge under addition.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh108.txt section 8.1 (addition and subtraction of algebraic expressions)

solution_steps.explain: One unlike term is a monomial, two a binomial, three a trinomial.

concepts.title: Multiplying Monomials
concepts.definition: Multiplying monomials multiplies the coefficients and adds the exponents of matching variables: 3x times 5x squared gives 15x cubed, and three or more monomials chain the same way.
concepts.key_idea: Numbers multiply, letters add their powers: coefficient times coefficient.

concepts.title: Multiplying a Monomial by a Binomial
concepts.definition: Distributing a monomial over a binomial hits every term: x times (a + b) becomes x times a plus x times b, so multiplying monomial by binomial or trinomial simply spreads the product across all inside terms.
concepts.key_idea: Everybody inside the bracket gets multiplied - distributivity in action.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh108.txt sections 8.4-8.4.2 (multiplying a monomial by polynomial)

solution_steps.explain: The monomial multiplies the first term of the bracket.
Each term inside receives the monomial.
The products add to give the expanded expression.

concepts.title: Multiplying Two Binomials
concepts.definition: Two binomials multiply by pairing every term of the first with every term of the second - four products in all - and like terms among the four merge, as (a + b)(c + d) expands to ac + ad + bc + bd.
concepts.key_idea: Two times two products, then tidy the middle: every term meets every term.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh108.txt section 8.5.1 (multiplying a binomial by a binomial)

solution_steps.explain: Multiply each of its terms by the whole second binomial.
Four products appear from the two-plus-two terms.
Merge the middle terms to finish the product.

concepts.title: Standard Identities
concepts.definition: Special products become identities worth memorising: (a + b) squared equals a squared + 2ab + b squared, (a - b) squared equals a squared - 2ab + b squared, and (a + b)(a - b) equals a squared - b squared; they evaluate products and factorise expressions instantly.
concepts.formula: value = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b
concepts.key_idea: Three identities do the work of dozens of expansions.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh108.txt section 8.6 (standard identities and their use)
